note:
VERDICT: InfraBuilder.cs itself was ALREADY CORRECT — no change made to it. The four exact-negation mismatches (INFRA_TUNNEL_FIRSTPORTAL x/yaw, INFRA_TUNNEL_FIRSTRETAIN x/yaw, plus the same pattern on INFRA_RIVER_FIRSTPARAPET/FIRSTPIER/FIRSTLAMP, INFRA_BRIDGEFURN railFirstX/railFirstYaw and every INFRA_STREET_FIRST* line) were a PROBE bug in Assets/Editor/Probes/InfraFurnitureProbe.cs, not a port bug: that probe printed `-items[i].Position.x` / `-items[i].YawUnity`, but InfraBuilder.Make() (InfraBuilder.cs:75-83) already mirrors through GeoFrame.ToUnity/YawToUnity exactly ONCE, so the probe's extra `-` was a SECOND mirror that cancelled the first and silently printed the raw GAME-frame coordinate instead of the Unity-frame one tools/_probe_infrabuilder.mjs's JS side expects (that JS side applies its own single `-x`/`-ang` as a documented stand-in for GeoFrame.ToUnity/YawToUnity, since there is no real GeoFrame.cs to call from Node). This matches the project convention exactly: RoadBuilder.cs's own class doc states 'Kit-piece PLACEMENT (InfraBuilder) is different [from RoadBuilder/BuildingBuilder/BridgeBuilder's per-vertex-mirror-at-mesh-build convention]: those meshes arrive pre-mirrored by the FBX importer..., so only the placement transform needs GeoFrame.ToUnity / YawToUnity' — i.e. InfraBuilder is SUPPOSED to take game-frame inputs and mirror once on output at Make(), which is exactly what it does.

Why the two x mismatches flipped in OPPOSITE directions (portal x: js negative/cs positive; retain x: js positive/cs negative) is fully explained by this single bug and nothing else: portal x's underlying raw game value is +100 (mouth.X=100 directly), so js prints -100 (single mirror) while the double-negated cs printed back the raw +100; retain x's underlying raw game value is -3 (cx = m.X - m.Dx*back = 0-3), so js prints +3 (single mirror of a negative) while cs's double negation printed back the raw -3. Same bug, different sign of the same underlying raw coordinate — not two different bugs and not evidence the mirror is applied an inconsistent number of times.

Non-degenerate yaw proof (the brief explicitly disallows using the ±π underpass case as evidence, since -π and +π are the same rotation): INFRA_TUNNEL_FIRSTPORTAL's yaw comes from mouth.Ang=0.5 rad, nowhere near a multiple of π. Before the probe fix: js printed yaw=-0.500000 (single mirror, correct Unity value), cs printed yaw=0.500000 (double-mirrored back to the raw game value) — an exact, non-degenerate-yaw mismatch that proves YawToUnity was being applied an even number of times net (0 or 2) by the PRINT statement on top of Make()'s one correct application. After removing the probe's extra negation, cs now prints yaw=-0.500000, matching js exactly.

sx/sy/sz: confirmed by reading src/infra.js (place(), infra.js:113-124; tunnel_portal, infra.js:246-249; underpass_wall taper, infra.js:264-272) that the JS NEVER assigns a negative sx/sy/sz anywhere — tunnel_portal's sx/sy/sz are all the same positive uniform mouth scale `m.s`, and underpass_wall's sx is a fixed positive 2 (a local-X stretch of the retaining-wall tile across the gap) with sy tapering between 0.5 and 1. These are LOCAL-SPACE stretch magnitudes along the kit mesh's own axes, applied after the mesh's own rotation/mirror, not a world-axis direction — so GeoFrame's X-mirror + FlipWinding already reorients the mesh correctly without the scale needing a sign flip, and InfraBuilder.Make()/FurniturePlacement.Scale correctly never negates sx/sy/sz. A negative sx would flip winding a SECOND time and render the headwall inside-out, which the JS never does and the C# correctly never introduces.
verified: node tools/_probe_infrabuilder.mjs (after fixing the probe's own INFRA_RIVER_FIRSTPARAPET/FIRSTPIER/FIRSTLAMP lines to apply the same single -x/-ang mirror every other section already applied, so the river section actually exercises handedness instead of coincidentally matching a double-mirrored value) vs. the real Unity run: `pkill -f Unity.app/Contents/MacOS/Unity; sleep 2;` then `/Applications/Unity/Hub/Editor/6000.6.7f1/Unity.app/Contents/MacOS/Unity -batchmode -quit -nographics -projectPath unity -executeMethod TbilisiFly.Probes.InfraFurnitureProbe.Run -logFile /tmp/infra_fixed.log`, compared with `python3 tools/unity_port_check.py /tmp/infra_js_fixed.txt /tmp/infra_fixed.log`. Result: PASS - 65 values match to float32 precision (worst relative difference 7.926e-08, i.e. float32 rounding noise, at INFRA_RIVER_FIRSTPARAPET). All 8 count fields (portals=2, underpass=28, kerbs=76, crossings=2, signals=2, busstops=2, guardrails=100, manholes=1) matched both before and after — they were never affected, since a sign flip doesn't change a count. Only the position/yaw VALUES needed the probe fix; InfraBuilder.cs's 374 lines were read in full and left unmodified.
